newsitem.title: USA: Iowa corn, soy planting near complete, slow growth.
newsitem.headline: Iowa corn, soy planting near complete, slow growth.

text.p: Corn and soybean planting were nearly complete in Iowa in the week ended on Sunday but emergence was behind normal due to cool weather, the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service report.

Low temperatures statewide dropped to 30 degrees F at Spencer and Decorah at midweek. Rains entered northern Iowa from Thursday but dry weather allowed rapid planting progress on other days, the agency said.
Corn was 99 percent planted versus 94 last year and 87 on a five-year average, while emergence of the corn crop remains about 3 days behind average at 67 percent, the agency said.
Soybeans were 87 percent planted versus 52 last year and 58 average, while emergence at 16 percent was also about three days behind the normal pace, it said.
Oats were 95 percent emerged, ahead of the average pace of 91 percent, with the crop rated 69 perecent good to excellent and 29 percent fair.
Winter wheat condition improved with the crop rated 80 percent good to excellent, up from 67 percent last week, and 18 percent fair.
Pasture conditions were rated 7 percent excellent, 45 good, 34 fair, and 14 poor as of Sunday.
Topsoil moisture was rated 2 percent surplus, 68 adequate, and 29 short, while subsoil moisture was rated 6 percent surplus, 87 percent adequate, 7 percent short.
